107.t: Back in Detroit and hired by Count Basie
107.s: Back in uniform in May 1953 he learned Basie was looking for him and joined the band on July 27, 1953.
107.ch: Joining and playing in the Basie band
107.q: And after being released and shipped back to the United States, I came back to Detroit, now this was May of 1953. My first day in town, I don’t have any civilian clothes, I’m walking around in my Army uniform, I ran into an old friend who said, “Count Basie is looking for you.” I said, “Count…

107.t: Reading Down Beat, discharge and the Detroit audition for Basie
107.s: He saw Basie in Down Beat in February 1953, left the army in May, and auditioned at Detroit's Graystone Ballroom on Body and Soul and Perdido.
107.ch: Joining Basie and life on the road
107.q: Yes. In February of 1953 -- I was scheduled to be released in May, so in February of 1953 I got a hold of a Down Beat magazine. I saw a picture of the Basie orchestra with inset photos of Paul Quinichette and Eddie “Lockjaw” Davis. I remember saying to myself, “Man, I sure would like to be in that…

107.t: Recalling the audition and flying to New York
107.s: Opening the second session, Foster restates the audition, Basie's 'we'll be in touch kid', and the telegram in July.
107.ch: Joining Basie and life on the road
107.q: I think I’ve already said that I walked into the auditorium -- not auditorium, but dancehall. The band was playing. I walked up to -- Ernie Wilkins and Jimmy recognized me immediately. They -- I suppose introduced me to Basie. I don’t remember the moment I was introduced to Basie. All I can…

107.t: The Sunset Terrace night and the 'Basie miracle'
107.s: A sick-drunk Foster made the Collegians' Indianapolis date; Eckstine, Sarah Vaughan and Dexter sat in, and Eckstine's later recommendation led to Basie in 1953.
107.q: I feel it’s very important, especially because of the connections that were made and the strange way in which it came about. The band, the Wilberforce Collegians was to make one of it’s more important trips to Indianapolis, Indiana. It was to be at a place called the Sunset Terrace, which plays its…

1016.t: The audition tape and first rehearsal with Maynard's band
1016.s: He borrows a baritone, sends a tape, moves home to Philly in ten days and plays his first read of Blue Birdland.
1016.q: Yeah. Oh. Well he was the one who got me on. Eric came down and he had that — he was a great player. And he said, “Look, they’re going to be looking for a bari player, and I had a tenor, I didn’t even play bari. And I said okay. All right. I mean this is a whole, stop me whenever you want because…

1016.t: Joining Maynard's band: being ready and how Eric Traub got him the call
1016.s: Asked about a Japan video of Salt Peanuts, he explains how a Miami friend, Eric Traub, tipped him to the Maynard Ferguson baritone opening.
1016.q: Yeah, there’s a certain amount of yes to that I think yeah, but Maynard was, I mean this is a lot about Maynard but there’s not a day that goes by that I don’t think about this guy since I’ve been off the road because it was such an influence in a lot of different ways. So going back to that being…

900.t: Leaving Rock Island and auditioning for Disney in Miami
900.s: Encouraged by Charlie Teagarden, he auditions in Miami with Jack Keller, Ray McKinley and Chubby Jackson and is offered a Disney spot.
900.q: And I really took to it. Because I hadn’t even started seventh grade yet was when our band program started. There was no sixth grade music back in 1940 something. And so I was playing “Jam On Home” you know which was bad for me because for me reading music came second or something I had to learn to…

206.t: Auditioning for Dick Stabile in Pittsburgh
206.s: He auditioned with 'Confessing' and had to buy a trumpet to join Stabile.
206.q: Yeah. Dick Stabile — there was a trumpet player from Buffalo by the name of Joe Gustafaro, who — which, Dick was leaving the band and of course the news got around. And my brother drove me to Pittsburgh to, in essence, audition. All I did was Dick said,

606.t: Meeting Oscar Peterson in Buffalo and joining his trio
606.s: A trio formed from Jimmy Dorsey band members played a Buffalo hotel, where Peterson sat in; four years later he asked Ellis to join.
606.q: I was playing, I had been with bands, I’d been with Jimmy Dorsey, and the three of us in Jimmy Dorsey’s band, the bassist and the pianist and myself formed a trio, sort of a la Nat Cole, and we were playing in Buffalo. And we played in the same hotel for, oh months at a time. And the people from…

1020.t: Maynard Ferguson's band and the road to Weather Report
1020.s: Erskine calls Maynard the best boss, says the loud band prepared him for Weather Report, which he got because Jaco heard him.
1020.q: Yeah. Maynard’s band was loud. And I had turned it down three times I think when he called, because I wanted to finish school. And fans will forgive me for saying this but I used to view Maynard’s band as a bit of a three ring circus you know, and his being generous and highlighting the sidemen, it…

540.t: How his mother's connections led to the Basie audition
540.s: Through Hampton University and Aaron Woodward, Frank Foster called Gardner; his first gig in Newark turned out to be the audition.
540.q: That would have to be the time when I joined the Basie band. As fate would have it, my mother got me the gig. Can you imagine that? My mother at the time was chairperson of the music department at Hampton University in Hampton, Virginia. And I was in grad school at Indiana University with Mike…

835.t: Replacing drummer Steve Bohanon in the Ellis band
835.s: Humphrey fakes his way through the charts, is invited to audition in Los Angeles, and learns he is replacing the drummer who was leaving for the service.
835.q: Yeah, there were. When I first saw the band it was two drum sets and percussion. And the main drummer, his name was Steve Bohanon, and he died at age 21 tragically in a car accident. But he was going to leave the band anyhow to join the service. And Don needed a replacement for him, and so he was…

542.t: Getting the Maynard Ferguson call via Montmartre
542.s: A Maynard trumpeter sat in at Montmartre and passed his name on; telegrams, a tape starting with My Funny Valentine, and a Danish newspaper the day Lee Morgan was shot.
542.q: I was playing at a club called Montmartre in Copenhagen and this English trumpet player came in and asked if he could sit in. And it turned out he was Maynard’s lead trumpet player. And he was on vacation in Copenhagen and he said, “you know Maynard’s going to be looking for a baritone player soon…

938.t: How Noto got the Kenton job
938.s: A bus accident hurt Kenton's trumpeters in Buffalo and Noto was called to fill in.
938.q: Stranger things than that have happened.

656.t: Maynard Ferguson hears New Wave; Militello gets the baritone chair
656.s: Maynard heard the band at the Landmark; Mike Migliore recommended Militello, who borrowed a baritone and bought one at Manny's.
656.ch: Big breaks: New Wave, Maynard, Tony Bennett
656.q: Yeah. And we weren’t making any money at all. I think I made five grand that whole year. And I learned more and broke more plateaus in soloing and the understanding of jazz during that period I think, almost than during any period of my life. We were working at it and we were grooving. Absolutely…

459.t: How Shiner got the Sauter-Finegan audition
459.s: Eddie Irwin recommended him; he flubbed Moonlight on the Ganges but the band wanted him; band formed 1952.
459.q: They were auditioning musicians in New York when they started the band, and they said, “Does anybody know of any oboe doublers?” And this one trombone player said, “Yeah I know a guy up in Rochester.” Eddie Irwin, Eddie played in the New York Philharmonic. He says, “This guy doubles, he’s a good…

217.t: Sneaking into the Kirksville armory and sitting in with Jack Teagarden
217.s: He climbed through a window to hear Teagarden, sat in on Back Home in Indiana, and a month later got a telegram to join the band.
217.q: Well Jack Teagarden sent a telegram to the school. I was going to college in Kirksville, Missouri. And he sent a telegram. Well he’d been through and played a dance in the armory building in Kirksville, and I didn’t have the money to get in to hear Jack you know, but I knew Jack I mean through a…

823.t: Auditioning for Kai Winding after the Navy
823.s: He tells how he phoned Kai Winding, rushed to the rehearsal, played 'The Preacher', and was hired despite poor sight-reading.
823.ch: Kai Winding and New York studios
823.q: Yeah. Butterfield came first. I was actually, I had just gotten out of the Navy and actually, no they were sort of interspersed with each other I think, I take that back. I was just about to get discharged from the Navy when my brother and this funky girl that he was dating at the time came down to…

389.t: Joining the band, first rehearsal and heading to New York
389.s: He travelled to Massachusetts with his instruments, heard his arrangements played and was told of the Roseland engagement.
389.ch: With the Goldkette band: Bix and Trumbauer
389.q: As many as you could get, and "Bring it along." I guess this is the enticement, "Come on, bring them along, play them all," and so forth. Well, I had quite a problem getting up there with my bag and all my instruments and all I was loaded. And I had to change trains.
